paper_metadata.title: Enhancing Credit Risk Prediction through Co-trained Hybrid Quantum Transfer Learning Model

summary: The paper studies two gate-based quantum machine learning experiments on a Kaggle credit-risk dataset: a standalone 4-qubit QNN baseline and a co-trained hybrid quantum transfer learning model. The hybrid model achieves accuracy 0.9117, AUC 0.9134, and minority-class recall 0.73, improving over the standalone QNN's 0.8097 accuracy, 0.7446 AUC, and 0.16 minority-class recall, but the work is simulator-based and does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Hybrid co-trained quantum transfer learning model for binary credit risk classification, jointly training a classical feature extractor and a 4-qubit variational quantum circuit.

algorithm.variant: co-trained hybrid quantum transfer learning model
algorithm.ansatz: 4-qubit variational quantum circuit with angle encoding, entanglement layer, and trainable parameterized rotations; embedded via PennyLane TorchLayer
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 10 epochs; best performance at epoch 8

hyperparameters.feature_extractor: 3-layer MLP with ReLU and Tanh activations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical feature extractor compresses 24 input features to 4 latent features; each latent feature is encoded on one qubit using RY rotations
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of loan default vs non-default with binary cross-entropy loss

problem_instance.description: Credit risk prediction on a real-world Kaggle credit risk dataset

dataset_specification.description: 24 features, 32,580 instances; normalized with Min-Max scaling; unbalanced dataset used for final training; 80/20 train-test split with stratification

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: EDA performed; Min-Max scaling; SMOTE was evaluated but discarded because the unbalanced dataset gave better results; classical feature extractor used to reduce dimensionality before quantum encoding
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Test-set evaluation over 10 epochs; performance reported with accuracy, AUC, precision, recall, and F1-score; convergence curves shown

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Min-Max scaling; 3-layer MLP feature extractor; reduction to 4-dimensional latent space; end-to-end co-training of classical and quantum parameters

limiting_factors: Uses PennyLane default.qubit simulator rather than quantum hardware
